candidate_relations.label: Portal hypertension with hepatosplenomegaly and dilated portal and splenic veins
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes hepatosplenomegaly and dilated portal/splenic veins as imaging findings, which are consistent with portal hypertension as a complication of Niemann-Pick disease type B. However, the reference diagnosis is the underlying lysosomal storage disorder (NPD type B), which also explains the bilateral adrenal lesions, normochromic microcytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, dyslipidemia (low HDL, elevated triglycerides), family history of splenomegaly, and early-onset hypertension. C001 names only a downstream complication/manifestation rather than the root etiologic diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Portal hypertension with hepatosplenomegaly is a complication/manifestation of Niemann-Pick disease type B, not the underlying diagnosis itself

case_quality_flags: Niemann-Pick disease type B is a rare lysosomal storage disorder; bilateral adrenal infiltration, hepatosplenomegaly, dyslipidemia, and cytopenias together with family history are characteristic features supporting this diagnosis
Basal ganglia hemorrhage in context of thrombocytopenia and portal hypertension is a plausible complication rather than a separate etiology
